# ms-go-learning-planner

`ms-go-learning-planner` owns design-time learning goals, target/prerequisite graphs, gap analysis, course planning, content-generation orchestration, and replan decisions. It reads objective mastery from `ms-go-student`, generates each planned lesson through the typed confidential `course.lesson-content.v1` AI Prompt contract, asks `ms-go-course` to atomically reuse or persist the resulting private active Course, assigns it in Student, and replaces the Student-owned Learning Path.

There is no separate Knowledge Tree service in this architecture. Reviewed versioned goals, exact learning targets, prerequisites, and transition knowledge live here. `ms-go-teacher-agent` may recognize a desired outcome and requested skills, but it delegates the complete plan request to this service and never generates or persists Course structure itself.

`STUDENT_SERVICE_INTERNAL_TOKEN` is Student's general read token.
`STUDENT_SERVICE_LEARNING_PLANNER_TOKEN` and `COURSE_SERVICE_INTERNAL_TOKEN`
are the dedicated Learning Planner write tokens accepted by the owning
services. The Student read and write tokens must differ.

`TEACHER_SERVICE_INTERNAL_TOKEN` protects Teacher's delegated planning route.
It also protects the read-only graph-readiness route. That additive route is
disabled by default with `PLANNER_GRAPH_READINESS_ENABLED=false`; enable it only
after the compatible Student snapshot and neutral published graph are live.
`PRACTICE_TASK_SERVICE_INTERNAL_TOKEN` protects Practice-only route resolution
and lazy materialization. A practice route is resolved once from exact Step
requirements plus Student-owned mastery, then returned to Practice for storage
as a frozen snapshot. Missing material is generated only when explicitly
ensured and is persisted by Course as a reusable one-Lesson private Course.
Terminal `course.plan.completed` and `course.plan.failed` envelopes are
committed with the request in a PostgreSQL transactional outbox and published
at least once to `LEARNING_PLANNER_EVENTS`; `event_id` is the JetStream
deduplication key. Broker outages do not stop the HTTP service because the
publisher connects lazily and retries from the outbox.

## Local verification

```sh
./scripts/check-agent-policy.sh
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
go build ./...
```

See [service documentation](docs/README.md) for owned contracts and boundaries.

The included Compose file requires explicit internal tokens and never supplies
working shared-secret defaults. Follow the
[production rollout checklist](docs/rollout.md): provision
`LEARNING_PLANNER_EVENTS`, deploy AI Prompt, Course, and Student contracts first,
then start Planner and Teacher consumers.
